subject: Clarify: what we actually capture by default (requests, partial streams, function outputs) and erase process
messages:
From: Elsa Matthews <elsa.matthews@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick examples we can share with our audit team

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the call this morning. The BrightBank audit team asked for a short table of concrete examples we can give them showing what Redwood *does* keep by default vs what is ephemeral. They want examples that map to our product features (streaming, function/tool outputs, file uploads, conversation prompts).

Could you share 3–4 short scenarios we can include in the SOC memo (things like: streaming partial tokens before finalization; function responses that include third-party data; uploaded files referenced in a prompt; KV-cache for session resume) and which of those are deleted on customer request vs retained for troubleshooting/metrics? Also, what's the timeline for deletion if they request erasure and what evidence we can provide?

I attached a screenshot of the API call they want to reference and a draft retention table. If easier, happy to hop on 20 mins later today.

Thanks —
Elsa
Director, Cloud Security
BrightBank

Attachment: screenshot-api-call.png (image/png)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elsa Matthews <elsa.matthews@brightbank.com>
Cc: BrightBank Security <security@brightbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick examples we can share with our audit team

Hi Elsa —

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of concrete stuff the auditors want. Below I've sketched 4 scenarios with the default behavior and the erasure path. I kept the language short so you can paste into the memo. If you want a diagram or signed evidence, we can produce a csv excerpt and a signed letter from our compliance team.

1) Short chat prompt with model answer- Example: POST /v1/generate with body {"prompt": "Summarize Q4 results"} returns a single final completion.
- Default capture: request payload (prompt) and final output kept for up to 45 days (default hosted retention window).
- Streaming nuance: if client uses streaming, partial tokens are buffered in the runtime but only final stabilized output is stored as the canonical response; transient stream fragments used for in-flight routing are not kept beyond the request trace window (minutes) unless the request later becomes a stored record (e.g., archived export).
- Erasure: customer erasure request triggers removal of stored request and final output from primary data stores; tombstone/replica cleanup completes within 30 days. We provide a deletion token and a confirmation timestamp.

2) Function/tool call that returns external data- Example: model triggers a function to fetch account info and returns a structured JSON.
- Default capture: request metadata and the function output are stored as part of the session record by default; function call logs are retained to support observability and debugging.
- Sensitive-handling: we have optional redaction hooks and can mark function outputs as non-persistent during onboarding.
- Erasure: inclusion in erasure includes function outputs; if the function output references third-party content, we include it in the deletion evidence when present in our stores.

3) File uploaded during prompt (attachments)- Example: POST /v1/upload + prompt referencing file.pdf
- Default capture: file metadata (filename, size, MIME) and a pointer/reference to where the file is stored are captured; by default, files are stored in a customer-isolated blob with 90-day default retention for Hosted customers (configurable for Dedicated/Private).
- Erasure: file blob removal is coordinated with the blob store; deletion completion times depend on the underlying storage provider but we provide confirmation and a blob-id wipe log.

4) Session KV cache and resumable context- Example: long-running chat with KV cache used to speed up replays
- Default capture: KV cache entries are considered ephemeral artifacts used for inference optimization; they are not part of the canonical audit logs and have a short TTL (default 7 days).
- Exceptions: if the session is explicitly snapshot/exported or the customer opts into transcript retention, snapshots become canonical and are retained per the standard retention window.

I'll loop in Rishi and Jonas for the exact timelines and the set of artifacts we can provide as deletion evidence. If you want, we can convert this into a one‑page diagram for the auditors.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Product Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines-retention-table.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Dec 2025 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick examples we can share with our audit team

+1 to Kim's writeup. A few concrete clarifications we should give BrightBank to avoid nitpicks: 

- Streaming: operational traces (tcp/tls level, per-request router traces) are short-lived and used solely for debugging; they are purged within 24 hours by default. Only stabilized outputs (final completion or explicit archive) are indexed into longer-term stores.
- Function outputs: we log the function invocation event and the returned payload; if the payload contains PII the customer can configure the connector to redact before storage. For Hosted accounts we default to storing function outputs to aid in dispute resolution; Dedicated/Private customers can opt out.
- Attachments: we should point auditors to the blob wipe procedure (we have E2E wipe for S3-compatible backends; GCP/Azure timings differ). Mention that we provide a signed S3 deletion manifest on request for accounts on those providers.
- Evidence package: we can provide a CSV with record ids + deletion timestamps, and a signed statement from Compliance that deletion occurred. The deletion token Kim mentioned is generated as a UUID and maps to our internal erasure job.

I'll prepare the short evidence checklist (csv + manifest + statement) and can produce a sample redaction config for function outputs if they want to limit capture further.

-Rishi
Senior Privacy Engineer

Hi Elsa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a one‑page summary and an example evidence checklist we'll send when BrightBank requests erasure proofs. For the memo, feel free to use the four scenarios as-is.

Summary of key timeline points to include in your audit memo: 
- Default hosted retention window for canonical requests/outputs: 45 days.
- Transient streaming traces and router-level logs: purged within 24 hours.
- KV cache TTL (default): 7 days unless snapshot/exported.
- Blob / attachment deletion: wipe manifest provided; completion depends on underlying provider but we confirm via deletion manifest within 30 days for Hosted S3-backed stores.

Evidence we can provide on erasure: deletion token, CSV of deleted record ids + timestamps, signed deletion manifest for blobs, and an attestation letter.

If BrightBank wants to tighten defaults (shorten retention, opt-out of function-output capture, or require immediate blob zeroing), we can propose a contract amendment and flag as a Dedicated/Private configuration.

I'll send the one-page PDF and the sample CSV to your security mailbox shortly. Happy to walk the auditors through this live — suggest a 30-min slot next week.

Best,
Kim

Attachments: rb-retention-onepage.pdf (application/pdf), evidence-checklist-sample.csv (text/csv)
